title: Credit Tier and Autopay Absorption for Trade-In Roll-Ins
content:
Two features of the buyer's contract under **Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts**, taken together, set the standing absorption share of a **Trade-In Agreements** roll-in: the minimum credit score of the contract's finance tier, and whether autopay is enrolled on the contract. The contract read is the one on the purchase the trade is applied to.

## Rule

| Tier's minimum credit score | Autopay enrolled on the contract | Standing absorption share |
|---|---|---|
| Below 640 | No | 0.8 |
| Below 640 | Yes | 0.9 |
| 640 or above | No | One (no reduction) |
| 640 or above | Yes | One (no reduction) |

The share multiplies the negative equity rolled in. It acts once on that amount, before the amount is held to no more than the finance tier's maximum negative equity and before the rounding to the nearest cent.

## Boundary

A tier whose minimum credit score is 639 is below the standing score line of 640; a tier whose minimum credit score is exactly 640 is at the line and takes no reduction.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

Negative equity of $1800.00; the linked contract sits in a tier with a minimum credit score below 640 and autopay is enrolled: $1800.00 multiplied by 0.9 is $1620.00. Without autopay it would be $1800.00 multiplied by 0.8, which is $1440.00.
